text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

- Leif Eide, market operations manager at the central bank, says there is no reason why Norwegian money-market rates should be higher than German ones. Speculation that the central bank will cut official interest rates soon is increasing among analysts and dealers.

-Nobody has applied for the vacant position as doctor at Norway's largest prison, Ullernsmo. Managing Director Knut Eigum at Ullernsmo says ailing prisoners will be transported to hospital only in emergencies.
-State-owned mobile phone company Telenor Mobil will most probably have one million costumers shortly, after a year of record sales of mobile phones.

-Norwegian shipper John Fredriksen has ordered a new drilling and production ship from the South Korean shipyard Daewoo worth 800 million crowns. Fredriksen has not signed any contract for the ship yet, but he says interest in the project is extensive.
-Fokus Bank, Norway's third largest commercial bank, says there are too many players in the country's overbanked financial community.
